title: The State Pension Is Enough to Live On? Alone, You're Over £1,300 a Year Short 😬👴 #shorts
description:
Retire alone on the full State Pension, and you're over £1,300 a year short.

The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week in 2026/27: about £12,500 a year (£12,547.60 over 52 weeks). That's under the £12,570 Personal Allowance, so with no other income no income tax is due on it.

Pensions UK's Retirement Living Standards (June 2026) say a Minimum retirement lifestyle costs £13,900 a year for one person, after tax. On the State Pension alone that leaves you £1,352.40 a year short (over £1,300). To cover the gap from a taxable private pension, Pensions UK puts the before-tax figure at £14,232 a year, about £1,684 on top of the State Pension.

The twist: a couple needs £22,500 for the same Minimum, not double (£27,800). Two full State Pensions pay £25,095.20, over £25,000, so a couple clears the Minimum by about £2,595 while someone alone doesn't. For a Moderate lifestyle (£32,700 for one person), the full State Pension covers only about 38%.

And that's before rent: the standards assume you own your home outright. Rent and mortgage payments are not included (council tax and household bills are). Figures are for outside London.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/new-state-pension/what-youll-get · https://www.gov.uk/income-tax-rates · Pensions UK, Retirement Living Standards update, 3 June 2026: https://www.pensionsuk.org.uk/Press-Centre/Press-Releases/Article/Retirement-Living-Standards-update-shows-the-nation-is-not-saving-enough- · https://www.retirementlivingstandards.org.uk/details
